text:
Logan Thompson was the difference at Capital One Arena. He faced 22 shots and stopped 21, which saved 1.89 goals more than the chances against him deserved, and that kept WSH level after Alexis Lafrenière's power-play snap shot put NYR up 1-0 in the first period.

WSH had the better of the play, generating 4.48 expected goals to NYR's 2.89, and in a simulated replay of every shot they win 55 percent of the time. Timothy Liljegren tied it in the second on a slap shot that carried only a 3 percent chance of scoring, and Boone Jenner put WSH ahead late in the period at 17:38. Jenner also had the night's best chance that didn't go in, a 35 percent look in the first period that Igor Shesterkin stopped.

The third period belonged to NYR on the shot map, with a 1.10 to 0.58 edge in expected goals, but they could not turn it into a goal. With the clock at 19:59, Tom Wilson scored on an 84 percent chance, with Vincent Desharnais assisting, to make it 3-1. NYR went 1 for 3 on the power play and WSH went 0 for 3, so the special teams did not separate them. WSH gave the puck away 19 times to NYR's 9, yet it was Thompson, the first star, who made that sloppiness cost nothing.
